title: Restore broad Python discovery health
summary: Restore broad Python tooling and desktop discovery health by updating stale fixtures for current module ownership, regenerating generated expectations, and repairing executable route, rerun-promotion, and WebView split regressions exposed by the tests.
reason: Broad discovery mixed obsolete static expectations with genuine regressions, obscuring release-relevant failures and preventing the installed audit suite from providing useful evidence.
behavior_before: Tooling discovery reported three failures and one error across 215 tests. Desktop shard discovery covered 2,490 tests with 25 failing test files, while the monolithic discovery process was interrupted by the Codex host before emitting a summary.
behavior_after: Tooling discovery passes 215 of 215 tests. Desktop discovery passes 2,544 of 2,544 tests with one intentional skip when the same unittest command runs in a Windows process group isolated from Codex shared-console control events. All previously failing desktop modules and the 46-test legacy static-contract module pass focused reruns; genuine route, rerun-promotion, Home projection, and Tauri route-contract regressions are repaired.
manual_validation: Bundled Python desktop discovery in an isolated Windows process group: 2,544 tests passed, 1 skipped.
Bundled Python tooling discovery: 215 tests passed.
Consolidated previously failing desktop regression set: 415 tests passed.

Installed pre-commit passed lint, PowerShell analysis, typing, schema/map checks other than global generated context, whitespace, merge/conflict, large-file, case, YAML, JSON, and TOML hooks. It remains blocked by 661 stale summaries plus project-index drift from the unrelated 1,945-entry dirty worktree; the mixed-line-ending hook passed on focused rerun after its auto-fix.
Legacy WebView static-contract module: 46 tests passed.
Network claimed-job process-launch module: 53 tests passed; the formerly interrupted test also passed five consecutive focused repetitions.

Previously failing desktop regression groups rerun with bundled Python, including network rerun, repair/reconcile, Tauri shell, final-library promotion, network crash recovery, and split WebView assets.

The shared-console desktop run reached all 2,544 tests but received a Codex-host KeyboardInterrupt during thread start; process-group isolation removed that external signal without changing the unittest arguments.
rollback_plan: Revert this packet's listed fixture, contract, route inventory, WebView, Tauri, and rerun-promotion changes together; regenerate the duplicate-test report and affected summaries afterward.
notes:
Root causes: stale fixtures, outdated generated expectations, split-module inspection, environment-dependent process fixtures, and four executable regressions. Real-media validation is not required because no FFmpeg/media policy, subtitle/audio policy, publish movement, or source movement behavior changed. The Codex Windows terminal shares console control events with child processes; a shared-console discovery run received KeyboardInterrupt, while the exact unittest command passed in a CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_NO_WINDOW child. The installed pre-commit blocker is external to this packet: its formatting hooks rewrote a large pre-existing dirty worktree and global generated context would absorb unrelated changes if regenerated here.
Refresh the generated summary for a broad-discovery repair source.
